Short answer: not as a regular habit, and not without supervision. At 16 you can build serious strength without ever testing a true one-rep max. Heavy sets of 3 to 5 reps with clean technique tell you nearly the same thing and carry far less risk.

If you do want to test a max at some point, do it with a coach or an experienced adult spotting you, in a rack or with safeties, after a proper warm-up, and only on lifts where your technique is solid. A good time to build toward it is once you have a few months of consistent training behind you, not as a first-week experiment.

Talk it over with your parents and a coach at your school or gym too. If you tell me which lift you're curious about, I can help you work out how to tell where you're at without going to a true max.
